data.title: Drag-to-Annotate & Frozen Frame
data.goalStatement: The core capture interaction: click-and-drag on the live mirror renders a dashed red outline with a live device-pixel size label and ruler/tick guides; release freezes the exact current frame and stages a numbered annotation anchored to the box. On the frozen frame everything outside annotation boxes dims and each annotation gets a popover (numbered badge, autofocused 'What's wrong here?' comment field, delete control, size/position meta line) with Enter to save and delete to remove and decrement the staged count. When popovers would crowd or overlap, they relocate to a gutter/sidebar panel linked to their boxes by leader lines. Why: this is the interaction that replaces 'screenshot plus prose description' and is the single most differentiating surface of the product.
data.rawDescription: The core capture interaction: click-and-drag on the live mirror renders a dashed red outline with a live device-pixel size label and ruler/tick guides; release freezes the exact current frame and stages a numbered annotation anchored to the box. On the frozen frame everything outside annotation boxes dims and each annotation gets a popover (numbered badge, autofocused 'What's wrong here?' comment field, delete control, size/position meta line) with Enter to save and delete to remove and decrement the staged count. When popovers would crowd or overlap, they relocate to a gutter/sidebar panel linked to their boxes by leader lines. Why: this is the interaction that replaces 'screenshot plus prose description' and is the single most differentiating surface of the product.

functionalRequirements.text: Support click-and-drag on the live mirror to draw a selection box, rendering a dashed red outline, a live device-pixel size label, and ruler/tick coordinate guides during the drag.
On drag release, freeze the exact current frame and create a new staged annotation anchored to the drawn box.

On a frozen frame, dim everything outside annotation boxes and show a per-annotation popover with a numbered badge, an autofocused free-text comment field (placeholder 'What's wrong here?'), a delete control, and a size/position meta line; Enter saves, clicking the delete control removes the annotation.
When annotation popovers would crowd/overlap, relocate them to a gutter/sidebar panel connected to their boxes via leader lines.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Live mirror glass-to-glass latency should stay low enough (target under ~150ms) that drag-to-select and freeze feel responsive.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given live mirror is streaming, when the user drags on the mirror, then a dashed red outline, live pixel-size label, and ruler guides render in real time.
When the user releases the drag, then the exact frame is frozen and a new staged annotation is created anchored to the drawn box.
Given a frozen frame with one annotation, then everything outside the box dims and a popover with numbered badge, autofocused comment field, delete control, and meta line appears.
Given an annotation popover is focused, when the user presses Enter, then the comment saves; when the user clicks the delete control, then the annotation is removed and the staged count decrements.
Given three annotations are drawn close together, when their popovers would overlap, then they relocate to a sidebar/gutter panel connected via leader lines.

scenarios.title: Draw and freeze a single annotation
steps: Drag on the live mirror to draw a box
Release to freeze the exact frame
Type a comment and press Enter to save

scenarios.title: Multiple crowded annotations relocate to gutter
steps: Draw three annotation boxes close together
Popovers relocate to sidebar gutter with leader lines

userStories.iWant: to drag a box directly on the live mirror and have the exact frame freeze on release
userStories.soThat: the bug is captured at the precise moment and region I saw it

userStories.iWant: an autofocused popover per box where I can type what's wrong, press Enter, or delete the box
userStories.soThat: I can flag several bugs in one pass without breaking flow
